newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Fiat workers suspend protest.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Fiat workers suspend protest.

text.p: Workers at an Italian Fiat SpA motor and gearbox plant in the Argentine province of Cordoba on Tuesday agreed to suspend their six-day-old occupation of the autoparts factory and try to reach a deal with management in 15 days, Fiat said.

"Production will return to normal as of tomorrow. We gave the workers a day off today as they were visibly exhausted by their protest," Fiat's local institutional relations manager Jorge Rendo told Reuters. "Now we have 15 days to negotiate. There is a good atmosphere for a good negotiation between the company and the workers."
Unions agreed to suspend their occupation after Cordoba's provincial government ruled that workers must return to work for a compulsory period of negotiation to end the dispute.

The conflict broke out last Wednesday after Fiat transferred workers from a related company's car plant and demanded that they accept the same conditions as its own workers. Rendo warned on Monday that Fiat could import gearboxes and engines from Brazil and Italy to replace Argentine production if the protest dragged on.
